text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The general manager of the Jiu Valley coalfield was taken hostage by some 3,000 miners after the administration failed to Easter bonuses, the paper says.
- The future trend of the national leu currency is unpredictable, the paper says.
- Trading of shares on the black market might affect companies.
- Floods disrupted rail and road traffic in the Hunedoara county, where the levels of the Mures river are on the rise.
- The fate of the troubled private banks Dacia Felix and Credit Bank will be decided by court ruling within the next months, the paper says.
- The State Ownership Fund has decided to liquidate the country's fishing fleet.
- The Association of car makers and importers will suspend a car show scheduled next month, following a decision by the transport ministry to levy a road tax on local motorists.
- Trade unions in the transport sector threatened to block roads and border crossings to protest against the new road tax.
- Floods affected 15,000 hectares in the Arad county.
